$comment: Router tiers for OmniRoute. Applied by apply.ps1 / apply.sh, which
validates every model against the live /v1/models catalog and skips
(with a warning) anything the catalog does not know.
tier1  = orchestrator: 1M-context, long-horizon. Models below 1M belong
in tier2 — the user-facing limit in opencode.jsonc says 1M.
tier2  = smart second level: strong reasoning, mid context.
tier3  = daily driver: cheapest capable codegen/review.
* -clean = same tier without models/plans that train on prompts: the
choice for sensitive data. See docs/models.md.
spark-1.3-contributor = pinned single-model route: the tier1 legs as a
standalone combo (zen free promo → openrouter paid), so callers
can address the spark family directly (incl. effort variants
like omniroute/spark-1.3-contributor#high) without pulling the
tier1 id's orchestrator semantics. Resolve order = combo order
rag = cohere RAG standby (trial keys, 128k, not in any tier): Command A → Command R Plus, address omniroute/rag directly.
gemini-3.8-flash = pinned single-model route: gemini free pooled head →
openrouter paid google-scoped payload. Free-first like spark.
Probe-falsified 2026-09-22: the BARE openrouter/gemini-3.8-flash
leg 400s ('not available in the active live catalog') — the
gateway's bare-name alias is not a provider ref, so only the
google-scoped twin ships. No 3.7 legs ever (version mixing is a
defect; 3.7-flash free input quota is also tiny).
deepseek-v4.1-flash = pinned single-model route: openrouter paid →
zen paid. Probe-falsified 2026-09-22: the deepseek-DIRECT leg
400s ('not available in the active live catalog for provider
deepseek'), so it was dropped; zen leg is real but 402s until
the Zen balance is topped up (chain hops by design). Exact model
only: no v4-flash (no suffix 1) or deepseek-flash legs
tier2-credit / tier3-credit = paid-credit burn chains: NO free heads, NO
strong-provider tails. They burn stored cerebras/sambanova/
partner credits when free tiers throttle, sparing deepseek-direct
/ openrouter / zen / meta money. Credit-first, not fallback-last.
A-D combos skip the LiteLLM config.yaml mirror and the global-litellm
tiers: the :4000 proxy adds nothing there (it cannot address gemini-free
heads, zen-free legs, or the cheaperinference reseller pool, and the
credit chains are gateway-native). Pinned single-model routes and
credit-burn chains live on the gateway only — enforced by the sync
contract (tools/sync-router-tiers.py ignores them), not by omission.
Role labels (display names only — tier1/2/3 ids are a contract and
never change: saved selections, --only flags and opencode.jsonc keys
all address them by id):
tier1 = orchestrator-1M      (long-horizon orchestration, 1M required)
tier2 = smart-reasoning-128k (strong reasoning, mid context)
tier3 = cheap-driver-128k    (cheapest capable codegen/review loop)
The same labels appear as opencode.jsonc model names and in the web UI
router-tiers card, so every surface explains itself the same way.
PER-MODEL FALLBACK ORDER: free-first, with a FAST-SKIP on a dead leg
(revised 2026-09-23, operator call). The zen free contributor promo is
the FIRST leg again: when it serves, spark costs nothing. It currently
refuses proxied traffic after a couple of calls ('OpenCode's free tier
can only be used from within OpenCode' — a 403), and a 403 is a
permanent-class error, so the gateway would retry it on EVERY request
unless the breaker opens. `providerBreaker.apikey.failureThreshold` is
therefore set to 2 (apply.* does it): after two failures the opencode-zen
connection is skipped for resetTimeoutMs (30s) and the chain goes
straight to the paid contributor leg, then retries zen on the next
cooldown expiry. Free when it works, at most two cheap round-trips when
it does not. The same threshold makes every other failing free leg hop
fast instead of being retried ~12 times.
Why this also fixed a confusing client error: a 15s
requestQueue.maxWaitMs was killing spark mid-think, so the chain fell
through to this dead zen leg and the client saw the LAST leg's error
(an uncurated gemini free-tier 429). apply.* now sets maxWaitMs=180000
as well; see docs/verification.md for the full chain.
Per-model free→paid chains: each free leg is followed, further down the
same combo, by its paid twin on the same or a sanctioned provider, so a
quota-exhausted free leg degrades to paid instead of failing:
spark free (zen contributor-free) → openrouter contributor (paid).
The plain muse-spark-1.3 is BLOCKED operator policy 2026-09-21:
no combo may reference it; the contributor is the only spark.
gpt-oss free (groq) → cerebras/sambanova credit overflow, then the
chain moves to deepseek flash (openrouter/deepseek direct) → zen
paid, so every family still lands on a paid leg;
qwen3.8 free (groq) → cerebras credit overflow;
mistral-code/small free pool → mistral direct (same key bills past
the free pool) → deepseek/zen paid. Direct-key legs (mistral, deepseek)
are their own paid overflow: once the free pool is spent the same key
is billed, so no extra twin entry is needed for them.
tier1 is spark-only by design (2026-09-20): gemini-3.1-pro was dropped
because it reasons worse than gemini-3.8-flash while costing a 1M slot —
a weaker model in the orchestrator tier is a defect, not a fallback.
No 1M-context replacement is currently sanctioned, so tier1 degrades
within the spark family instead of hopping to a weaker family.
xhigh is caller-side reasoning effort, not a model ID: opencode callers
use the #high variant (omniroute/tier1#high, ack-proven), Zed sets
reasoning_effort xhigh (lib/**/install.*). The tier1-orchestrator agent
in opencode.jsonc pins omniroute/tier1#high.
Effort clamp (heterogeneous tiers): ladders are non-contiguous per
model (spark minimal..max, gemini low/med/high only, deepseek
none/low/high/max). A combo NEVER forwards an effort its head leg
rejects: clients clamp xhigh->high and minimal->low before tier2, and
Zed/OpenHands use the static effort aliases from sync-ide-models (e.g.
gemini-3.8-flash-high). A 400 'invalid reasoning_effort' is a clamp
bug, not a provider outage — do not add fallback legs for it.
*-clean = privacy tiers: NO free legs at all. Assumption: any big free
model may train on prompts, so clean chains use paid legs only.
tier1-clean: openrouter contributor (paid). PRIVACY DOWNGRADE
operator decision 2026-09-21: contributor legs TRAIN by contract,
so tier1-clean no longer means trains-nothing — it means paid-only.
The plain paid spark (trains nothing) was removed with the
contributor-only block. Meta-direct paid spark stays out:
unregistered 2026-09-23 (openrouter-first; muse-code 502s upstream).
tier2-clean: deepseek direct → openrouter paid deepseek → zen paid
flash → mistral-small direct. No groq/cerebras/sambanova free legs.
tier3-clean: deepseek direct → mistral-small direct → zen paid flash.
No qwen free legs. Lightweight paid review duty only.
cheap-inference is NOT a free pool: it is the user's own paid partner
gateway (own key, own billing), so its legs sit between free and paid
in tier2/tier3 — never in *-clean (privacy tiers stay direct-paid).
Contributor tiers (-contributor) are paid but TRAIN by contract ($0.10
pricing is the tell) — they stay out of tier2-clean/tier3-clean, and
since 2026-09-21 they are also the tier1-clean legs (operator
contributor-only block; see tier1-clean note above).
strategy 'priority' = try in listed order, next on 429/error: free legs
first, paid legs from cerebras/sambanova/deepseek/meta/openrouter/zen
after them (those paid tiers are explicitly allowed).
cheap-inference legs (cheaperinference/*) sit BETWEEN free and paid:
they are the user's own paid partner gateway, so quota-exhausted free
degrades to cheap-inference first, paid direct only after that.
Ref form is cheaperinference/<id> with the gateway's own model id
(e.g. cheaperinference/deepseek-v4-flash).
Retries before provider-hop ≈3 (2026-09-20): global requestRetry=3 /
maxRetryIntervalSec=30 (api settings get-api-settings), resilience
waitForCooldown maxRetries=3 / maxRetryWaitSec=30 (resilience status),
comboCooldownWait maxAttempts=5 / maxWaitMs=90s / budgetMs=300s (only
for transient non-quota reasons; quota_exhausted hops immediately).
The dashboard resilience knobs (resilience config set) cover breaker
thresholds only — retry counts live in the settings above. Keep the
wait short so a dead leg hops instead of stalling the run.
Model IDs verified against the live provider catalogs on 2026-09-20.
Cloudflare is registered but its Workers AI needs an Account ID in the
dashboard before it can serve; it is deliberately not in any tier yet.
Meta direct (muse-code) is registered but this OmniRoute build 502s on
it; spark goes through OpenRouter (contributor = trains, plain = clean).
groq and cerebras sit behind Cloudflare, which answers error-1010 to
Node's default UA - apply sets providerSpecificData.customUserAgent.
